name: Runway
tagline: The AI video lab pushing cinematic text-to-video and image-to-video generation forward.
tldr: Runway is an AI video generation platform best known for its Gen-4 and Gen-4.5 models, which focus on consistent characters, objects, and scenes across shots.
Best for filmmakers, agencies, and creative teams doing image-to-video, cinematic exploration, and short-form AI video production.

Runs on a credit-based subscription system (Standard, Pro, Max) that replaced its old $97/mo Unlimited plan in 2026, with different models (Gen-4, Gen-4.5, Gen-4 Turbo) consuming credits at different rates.
Used by companies like Netflix for parts of production workflows, and positioned as one of the more 'professional grade' AI video tools versus consumer-facing competitors.
Common complaints center on how fast credits deplete, failed generations still consuming credits, and inconsistent output quality on certain prompts.

plans.name: Free
plans.notes: 125 credits/month (~25 seconds of HD video), watermarked output

plans.name: Pro
plans.notes: 2,250 credits/month; Gen-4.5 costs 25 credits/sec, Gen-4 costs 12 credits/sec

plans.name: Max
plans.notes: Replaced the old Unlimited plan in 2026; purely credit-based, no Explore Mode

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.notes: Dedicated infrastructure, API access, SSO, SOC 2 compliance, SLAs

pros: Gen-4/Gen-4.5 models are widely regarded as strong for character and scene consistency across shots
Fast iteration for creative exploration, especially image-to-video workflows
Used in real production pipelines (e.g. reported use by Netflix), lending it professional credibility
Free tier lets users test the tool with real (if watermarked and limited) output before paying
cons: Credit-based pricing burns through quickly on higher-quality models like Gen-4.5, and failed generations still consume credits
Trustpilot reviews frequently cite account suspensions for 'unusual usage patterns' with unresponsive support
Removal of the old flat-rate Unlimited plan pushed some heavy users toward more expensive or less predictable billing
Motion artifacts and inconsistent physics still show up in close-ups and complex scenes

sentiment.quote: I've just used this tool for a video and the result is truly incredible. All of that in the free version as well. Super sharp masking and so many cool effects to add. I've found my new video editing best friend.

I do not recommend Runway ML. The company removed its previous $97/month Unlimited plan and replaced it with a credit-based system. The platform frequently generates incorrect results even when prompts are clear and detailed, while still consuming credits for failed generations.
Paid $144 for annual plan. Banned after 3 weeks for 'unusual usage patterns.' Support refused refund.

bestFor: Filmmakers and agencies prototyping cinematic shots from text or images
Creative teams needing character/scene consistency across multiple generated clips
Studios and production pipelines experimenting with AI-assisted video workflows
Users who want access to multiple video models (Gen-4, Gen-4.5, Turbo) in one platform
hotTake: Runway ditched its beloved $97/mo Unlimited plan for a credit meter, and its own Trustpilot page is now flooded with users complaining that failed generations still burn credits.
